text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in Rome on Wednesday that the premiers of Hungary, Italy and Slovenia could meet together in Budapest this spring. @

- Canada and Thailand yesterday joined Argentina, Australia, New Zealand and the US in objecting to the high level of Hungarian agriculture subsidies. A senior Industry and Trade Ministry official said the Hungarian government continues to search for a negotiated solution.

- The European Commission last night dissociated itself from a statement issued earlier Wednesday which said it is unlikely that Central and East European countries will become full EU members before 2002. @

- National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi yesterday called for lenient treatment of Central and East European countries seeking EU membership, specifically, that they should not be immediately required to meet the Maastricht economic criteria.
- Smallholders Party and the Christian Democratic Party began joint preparations of the next governmental cycle when the two parties' presidents signed a pact cementing closer cooperation. @

- Environmentalist group Danube Circle quotes the January 14 issue of the Prague weekly Respekt as saying a plan to construct a hydropower plant at Esztergom has been put on the agenda of Hungarian-Slovak expert level talks, said Danube Circle executive Janos Vargha.
- Environment Minister Ferenc Baja yesterday inaugurated the third national park in the Great Hungarian Plain, along the banks of the Holt Koros at Szarvas.
- The current account deficit closed last November at $53 million, the National Bank of Hungary reports. @

- The Hungarian curent account deficit was "surprisingly low" last year at $1.5 billion, but is expected to grow by one-third this year, analysts of the London-based investment and market research company Nomura say.
- The bus maker Ikarus expects to manufacture 2,500 buses this year, generating revenues of HUF 80 billion, said managing director Gabor Szeles yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Reuters news agency announced yesterday that it will launch a Hungarian language news service to be called Reuters Investor. @

- The Ministry of Agriculture will propose at today's cabinet meeting that agriculture subsidies match 3 percent of GDP in the first half of the period remaining until Hungary's integration into the EU, and by at least 2 percent of GDP in the second half.
- Free Democrat president Ivan Peto said yesterdy that this weekend's party meeting should put a definitive end to the ongoing dispute over whether to leave the governing coalition. @

- Spyros Papas, programme director for the EBRD, has announced that the EBRD will set aside ECU 30 million over a seven-year span to finance a project for small and medium size enterprises in Hungary.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The finance director of the state television MTV said the organisation expects HUF 14 billion in advertising revenue this year. The satellite broadcaster Duna TV had revenues of HUF 3.8 billion last year. @
- Daewoo will raise the HUF 4.51 billion registered capital of the roller bearing works MGM in February, said Daewoo MGM manager Wook Jin Yoon.
